Third hackathon win this semester, and my first time touching space tech. Happy to announce that my team placed as runner ups (🥈) in the Hackers Track at the Space Coast Initiative Hackathon last weekend where we built Drift Zero, a system that detects satellite collisions before they happen and flags when satellites are acting suspicious. It answers two questions: What's going to happen? and Is someone making that happen? I worked on a big part of the Shield backend, the collision prediction engine. It pulls live satellite data from Space-Track, simulates where satellites will be in the next few minutes, calculates collision probability using NASA standards, and generates maneuver options with fuel costs and lifespan impact. I also handled integration between Shield and the 3D globe frontend. The hardest part was learning orbital mechanics well enough in 24 hours to build something that actually worked. I'd never touched astrodynamics before, but reading NASA documentation and getting collision math right under a deadline was an interesting experience. As Low Earth Orbit gets more crowded, operators need tools that predict collisions and detect bad actors. Building Shield was a crash course in how high the stakes are when you're protecting multi-million-dollar assets in space. Huge shoutout to my amazing teammates Taher Akolawala , Madhurishitha Boddu , Kushagra Katiyar , Nikhil S. , and Esha Gokulram for working with me on this crazy build. Big thanks to Ruchir Gupta and Groundswell Startups for organizing, and Derek Tishler and Shambavi Jayaramaiah at BoxMica as well as Sailesh Kadam at Databricks for the mentorship and guidance they provided. Github: https://lnkd.in/eeBQ3_jW ...more

From zero cybersecurity knowledge to winning the NextEra Cybersecurity Challenge track in 24 hours. I’ve made it a habit at hackathons to pick tracks I know nothing about and figure it out as I go. This time it was cybersecurity, and honestly, it might be my favorite build yet because of how great it turned out. We built UseProtechtion, an AI-powered malware analysis tool that takes a suspicious file and returns a full security report streamed live to a web dashboard. I built the agentic pipeline including the agents that handle static analysis, dynamic analysis and MITRE mapping in parallel, remediation generation, and final report compilation. Also handled the entire integration between the frontend and backend components. The biggest challenge was hitting Google ADK rate limits early on. We were planning to use it for the Google Cloud track, but had to pivot to Claude API mid-build. Instead of trying to fight the rate limits, we shifted focus entirely to the cybersecurity track and went all in on making UseProtechtion as strong as possible. Learned a ton about malware analysis, sandboxing, and threat intelligence in 24 hours. Huge props to my teammates, Kushagra Katiyar , Madhurishitha Boddu , and Esha Gokulram , for striving to take the W at HackUSF. Also thanks to Brad Ditrick , the NextEra Energy, Inc. Team, and Google Developer Group on Campus at USF - University of South Florida for hosting such a great event. 🏆 Winner: Cybersecurity Track (Sponsored by NextERA Energy) Devpost: https://lnkd.in/ekVMbAt4 GitHub: https://lnkd.in/emsc7brY ...more

A few weeks ago I got an email I wasn't expecting: an offer for a summer software engineering internship, rescinded two days later due to a company hiring freeze. I'd done the interviews, gotten the offer, and then it was gone. But it pushed me to keep building. Since then I've built three hackathon projects in three consecutive weekends: PatchLab (a multimodal game playtesting platform fusing video, facial emotion data, and Apple Watch biometrics), winning Most Innovative Use of Sphinx at Georgia Tech's Hacklytics; NeuroPhenotype (a rare disease diagnostic system fusing custom EEG hardware with biosignals and AI-powered clinical intake), built at Harvard HackRare; and Buddy: Lock In (a multiplayer AI study platform with real-time focus tracking), winning Best Gamification Project and Best Use of Blender at UF SASEHacks. And each week, I've continued to volunteer at Florida Community Innovation, a civic tech nonprofit, as the backend lead, helping other students build tools for social and community workers serving people in need. Still actively looking for a Summer 2026 internship in SWE, AI, or biotech. If you're building something interesting or know someone who is, I'd love to connect. ...more ...more

From "Never used Blender" to "Best Use of Blender" in 24 hours... Sound familiar?? I’m excited to share that just last weekend, my team and I just took home TWO wins at SaseHacks hosted by @Society of Asian Engineers (SASE) - University of Florida: 🏆 Winner: Gamification Track 🏆 Winner: Best Use of Blender Our project, "Buddy, Lock In!", tackles the challenge of gamifying a mundane task. We built a social 3D game space where up to 4 friends can "lock in" together, with personal avatars (pokemon themed) to keep you accountable, and live quizzes based on what you have studied previously in the session. My contributions to this project were in the blender aspects. I downloaded open source models, manipulated them in Blender for our needs, and using react, was able to create animations and particle effects for the avatars. I spent hours finding audio clips online and syncing them with the effects in order to make the Pokémon's calls as authentic as possible. Next I helped with connecting the 3D space within our webapp, joining it to the other aspects. Going into this, I had zero Blender experience. When I saw that there was a blender track, I immediately called up my teammates, proposing a rough idea of the project and that we HAVE to use blender. Huge shoutout to my teammates Nikhil Sangamkar and Abhay Dronavalli. We all had a blast working on the project! Also, a big thanks to Aidan Sakata and Bryson McGinley for their support and judging this event! Check it out! Devpost: https://lnkd.in/eCnPas-J Github: https://lnkd.in/eastgqFS ...more ...more

Should CS instructors use AI-generated instructional videos in classroom? We wanted to move beyond speculation and understand what students actually think. In our study, 170 computing students across two U.S. universities watched three short AI-generated instructional videos on Markdown created using Knowlify (YC S25) and shared their perceptions. Here are the key findings: • Students rated the videos highly for quality, accuracy, and usability. • Nearly half of the students could not confidently identify that the videos were AI-generated. • Despite these positive perceptions, students were much more cautious about broader adoption. Most still preferred instructor-recorded videos and expressed greater trust in human-presented content. • Students felt AI-generated videos were best suited for simple, supplemental, and highly visual topics, but less appropriate for complex, interactive, or discussion-based content. Our takeaway: AI-generated instructional videos show strong potential to complement computing instruction, but they are not a replacement for the instructor presence and interaction that students value most. A note on transparency: The videos were created using Knowlify, which provided early access to the platform and free credits. Knowlify had no role in the study design, data collection, analysis, or interpretation of the results. 📄 Preprint: https://lnkd.in/ecypCJkd Work done in collaboration with Esse Ciego , Shubbhi Taneja and Wilson Wong, PhD, MBA #ComputingEducation #AIinEducation #GenerativeAI

This month, I wrapped up my 𝐀𝐈 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐭 𝐁𝐮𝐢𝐥𝐝𝐞𝐫 𝐈𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐩 at GlobalLogic ! In this incredible program, I designed, built, and shipped an end-to-end industry-scale Agentic AI software solution: an AI-native Learning Management System allowing K-12 teachers in any course subject to build coursework custom-tailored to their own curriculum in seconds, automatically scored against their own rubrics with detailed feedback provided to students. This software saves teachers hours of their time, while providing students the instant grading and feedback they need to succeed in the course. Additionally, I participated in technical workshops on topics such as Agentic AI, the AIDLC, and Forward-Deployed Engineering, received cross-disciplinary mentoring from industry professionals, and attended the annual Hitachi Intern Summit where I saw firsthand how Hitachi is pioneering the future of industry-scale AI. Overall, this was a phenomenal internship experience, and I would like to thank Iuliia (Julia) Ishkov and Mariia Lavrentieva for organizing and facilitating this program, and Krishnendra Gautam for all of your support throughout the entire recruitment, onboarding, and internship process. I'm excited to see how GlobalLogic continues to build the future of industry-scale AI solutions!
